country.comment: Primary empirical case study conducted in eThekwini Metropolitan Municipality, South Africa; literature review on PDF pp. 2-3 briefly discusses indigent/poverty policies in Rwanda and Botswana as background context.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title, Abstract (Setting), and Introduction; PDF p. 3, Methodological issues (Participants)

effect_estimate.comment: Purely qualitative interview and document study; no quantitative point estimates, CIs, or p-values are reported beyond descriptive policy thresholds (6 kL/month free basic water, 150 kWh free electricity, ZAR 1,500/month income threshold, R250,000 and R500,000 property-value thresholds, 24-month review cycle).
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. Municipal officials report that while eThekwini Metropolitan Municipality's indigent policy provides up to 6 kL/month of free basic water and free solid waste collection/sanitation alongside 150 kWh of electricity (historically automatic for properties valued at R250,000 or below, and under the new policy extended up to R500,000 subject to socio-economic means-testing criteria and 24-month reviews), policy execution is ineffective because implementation is fragmented across separate municipal departments with differing policies, indigent register maintenance is undermined by fluctuating employment and lack of formal payslips among informal-sector workers, budgets are insufficient, public input is lacking, and beneficiary selection is compromised by delays, nepotism, political patronage, and corruption.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract (Results); PDF pp. 4-6, Findings; PDF pp. 6-8, Discussion and Conclusion and recommendations

mechanism_certainty.comment: Primary qualitative study appraised with CASP Qualitative Checklist (design ceiling = 2). Interviews with municipal officials across Water Services, Finance-Revenue Services, Customer Services, Strategy Office, and Deputy City Managers directly document how property-value thresholds, means-testing/payslip documentation barriers, indigent register maintenance, departmental fragmentation, and political discretion shape delivery of free basic water and sanitation support.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 4-8, Findings, Discussion, and Conclusion and recommendations

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines indigent eligibility thresholds based on property value (R250,000 extended to R500,000) and income/means-testing documentation (lack of formal payslips for informal workers), registration/re-registration and 24-month review procedures on the indigent register, implementation delays, scattered execution across separate municipal departments without a dedicated office, lack of public input, and discretionary political patronage/nepotism in beneficiary selection for tariff-subsidized free basic services.
